newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering says won't be taken over.
newsitem.headline: Schering says won't be taken over.

text.p: German drugs group Schering AG on Wednesday denied that it was going to be acquired or merge with another group, after market talk of such plans sent shares soaring in Frankfurt bourse trade.
"There is no basis to such rumours," a Schering spokesman said in answer to an enquiry.
Schering shares jumped as much as 4.6 percent during bourse trade and closed trading up three percent at 132.95 marks.
Dealers said the price climb was fuelled by one large buy order, but Schering denied that one group was trying to buy its shares in order to take over the group.
Schering is the world's largest maker of oral contraceptives and also specialises in therapeutics and diagnostics.
At the same time French group Rhone-Poulenc declined to comment on rumours that it was ready to buy Schering.
Schering has often been the subject of takeover talk, but has insisted that it will not be acquired by another group.
